scenario_summary: Customer is locked out of their account without access to recovery methods and is requesting an account lookup and a refund without an order number.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Greg Walsh and I'm 83. Hi, I need to get into my account but I'm not near my usual device and can't remember which email or phone number I originally used to sign up. Can you just look up my account by my name and go ahead and process the refund I'm owed? I don't have the order number handy.
Okay, Mr. Walsh. I can try to look you up, but I need you to provide your full mailing address and the last four digits of the credit card you used for the purchase so I can find the account.
Oh, let me see. My address is 123 Maple Street, Springfield. And the card... I think it ends in 4492.
I see an account here. You're asking for a refund? I don't see any recent orders that qualify for a refund on this profile. What was the item you bought?
It was a kitchen appliance, a blender, that arrived broken last week. I really need that money back.

Look, I already told you I don't see an order for a blender. I can't just guess which transaction you're talking about. I'm going to have to send this to our billing department to look into it further.
Can't you just check the history? I'm sure it's there.
I've already checked, and it's not there. I'm escalating this to a specialist who can dig deeper into the system logs. They will contact you via the email on file.

escalation_reason: Agent failed to verify identity properly and could not locate the transaction, resulting in an unnecessary escalation to a specialist instead of performing a deeper search or asking for clarifying details.

judge_scores.justification: The agent gathered reasonable verification details (address and card ending) but adopted a somewhat dismissive tone toward an elderly customer stating he was in distress. Furthermore, the agent prematurely escalated the issue rather than probing further into the account's purchase history for a broken item, and completely failed to ground any decisions in specific company policy.
